batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 IDs and their supplied predictor outputs before measurement. Use controlled condition contrasts to extend the recent aminobenzonitrile and methyl-acetoacetate failure repairs, test other predicted response valleys, and resolve structural transfer across common carbonyl families. Include focused loading comparisons where existing measurements make the new label interpretable. Quantile spans and CW distances are secondary signals, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: Measure m160 at 5/1 and 150 ul, predicted 42.53/98.70 mL. The 50 ul observation ad833f34f6b91872362d was 44.72/101.17 after a very large acquisition-time underprediction. This tests whether the newly learned late response transfers across sample amount; the selected 2/1 condition supplies a matched ratio contrast.

Measure m160 at 2/1 and 150 ul, predicted 13.84/32.76. Together with selected 5/1 at the same loading and measured 50 ul endpoints in b21061720e23b7a5bdcb and ad833f34f6b91872362d, this tests whether amount changes the steep solvent-response slope or mainly shifts one endpoint.

Measure m161 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted 35.15/83.26. The measured 50 ul condition a60552f4d1a5ced4641f was 34.93/86.44. This challenges the current nearly amount-insensitive correction and, with selected 2/1 at 100 ul, tests its transfer over a controlled local curve.

Measure m161 at 2/1 and 100 ul, predicted 12.42/29.72. The matched 50 ul observation e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 was 14.22/31.49. Pairing this with selected 5/1 at 100 ul separates amount sensitivity from solvent sensitivity. The m160 pair uses a different amount and will be interpreted separately.

Measure m161 at 1/1 and 50 ul, predicted 6.14/16.35. This joins its measured 2/1 and 5/1 curve in e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f. Comparison with m160 at identical recorded conditions in a8ae74aecb3b1e85b73c tests where positional response differences emerge.

Measure m95 at 10/1 and 150 ul, predicted 11.40/35.38. Recent 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf9 measured 18.45/75.76 at 50/1, with finish underpredicted by 49.43 mL at acquisition. This interior label locates finish growth at the same amount, without assuming the high-ratio correction applies throughout the curve.

Measure m95 at 20/1 and 150 ul, predicted 13.42/52.50. With selected 10/1 and measured 50/1 in 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf9, this forms a fixed-loading three-point curve. It can distinguish gradual finish growth from a more localized transition and supervise V1 independently.

Measure ethyl acetoacetate m82 at 5/1 and 150 ul, predicted 9.75/25.00. Existing m82 measurements mainly cover stronger eluents, including 2/1 in 6b38c8782f95c673c809 at 50 ul. Paired with selected 20/1, this tests response transfer from methyl, tert-butyl and ether-containing acetoacetates while retaining their different recorded amounts.

Measure m82 at 20/1 and 150 ul, predicted 12.59/39.48. Its selected 5/1 condition supplies a controlled slope, and selected m95 and m25 at 20/1 provide related ester comparisons. Sample volume is shared across this comparison, but density-times-volume amounts differ and must remain model inputs.

Measure tert-butyl acetoacetate m25 at 20/1 and 150 ul, predicted 14.57/39.04. Its measured 5/1 anchor b6017da51a674177d16d is 8.11/16.69. This tests how ester-side-chain environment changes the response relative to selected m82 and m95, against the much later m107 5/1 observations.

Extend m27 to 20/1 and 100 ul, predicted 7.66/15.07. Recent c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc measured only 4.67/6.01 at 10/1, following 4.55/10.62 at 2/1 in 8748c66e5f0823e6a65e. This determines whether the current renewed finish growth is supported beyond that unexpected short interval.

Measure m27 at 10/1 and 150 ul, predicted 4.96/9.05. The measured 100 ul condition c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc finished at 6.01 mL. This focused amount contrast tests whether that short finish is confined to one loading condition and constrains how broadly its correction should transfer.

Measure m125 in neat EA at 50 ul with 500 ul DCM, predicted 5.08/11.94. The otherwise matched 300 ul observation 55f2352b50967352163e is 4.87/12.85. This tests whether the large volume associations measured at 1/1 and 2/1 disappear in stronger eluent, extending the ratio-dependent loading relationship with one label.

Measure m68 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 5.53/16.76. Its measured finish decreased from 25.62 at 5/1 in c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8 to 17.50 at 20/1 in cb534927304d5c892100. This interior condition locates the decrease and tests the predicted finish minimum, while onset remains near 6 mL.

Measure salicylaldehyde m197 at 2/1 and 100 ul, predicted 10.58/24.59. The selected 5/1 condition is predicted substantially earlier. A fixed-loading pair tests this unmeasured response valley; the measured 50/1 anchor 619663c2b3ffb3a6c497 establishes a later finish at a different amount.

Pair m197 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted 6.21/15.24, with selected 2/1. Ortho hydroxyl-carbonyl geometry could modify silica interactions, but does not establish the predicted decrease. These labels distinguish a real catalog relationship from another shared response-shape error after the aminobenzonitrile result.

Measure fluorinated phenol m209 at 2/1 and 100 ul, predicted 10.86/18.71. Its supplied measured anchor 2a7062ac85d66260b3be is in neat EA at 150 ul. With selected 10/1 at fixed loading, this tests the predicted low-ratio maximum on a phenolic graph lacking a carbonyl.

Measure m209 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 6.39/11.61, substantially earlier than selected 2/1. This tests whether the response valley extends beyond ortho hydroxyaldehydes to another phenolic environment. Either outcome supplies structure-dependent supervision in a sparsely measured condition region.

Measure bromosalicylaldehyde m190 at 2/1 and 100 ul, predicted 12.07/26.17. Selected 10/1 is predicted to finish earlier, whereas d1774335b45258bc173a measured 7.57/29.88 at 20/1. This tests whether an early maximum and later recovery are supported at constant recorded loading.

Measure m190 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 6.33/19.57. Together with selected 2/1 and measured 20/1 in d1774335b45258bc173a, this provides a three-point test of the predicted valley. Comparison with selected m197 examines bromine substitution, with the different recorded density retained.

Measure para-methoxybenzaldehyde m118 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted 9.46/25.84. Its measured 10/1 anchor 319e89d7000731f64e7f is 4.78/36.82, showing early onset and a much later finish. This tests whether the model incorrectly places onset growth before the observed finish expansion.

Extend m118 to 50/1 and 100 ul, predicted 19.60/48.19. With selected 5/1 and measured 10/1 in 319e89d7000731f64e7f, the label tests whether finish growth accompanies delayed onset or preserves early onset. Related methoxy carbonyl scaffolds show sufficiently different behavior to make this extrapolation informative.

Measure para-methoxyacetophenone m115 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted 11.96/26.12. Its measured 2/1 anchor f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0 is 10.02/19.89. Paired with selected 10/1, this tests where its predicted strong finish growth begins and supplies a ketone comparison to selected methoxybenzaldehyde m118.

Measure m115 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 16.42/42.84. Its selected 5/1 condition tests the same-loading slope. The ortho isomer m127 has finishes near 31–32 mL at 20/1 in 8143c4fff6f999b7ad0e and 15d6bc57a87392fbeb98; this label tests whether para substitution supports the predicted stronger response.

Measure formylphenyl acetate m28 at 5/1 and 100 ul, predicted 11.94/35.97. The matched 2/1 observation 5522a1ec1f8e39cedb13 is 6.27/25.12. This tests the response of a bifunctional aromatic aldehyde/ester, complementing methoxy carbonyl comparisons without treating acceptor count as an absolute retention rule.

Measure m28 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 18.27/47.11. Together with selected 5/1 and measured 2/1 in 5522a1ec1f8e39cedb13, this distinguishes a sustained response from a localized finish increase and teaches the two endpoint heads on an undercovered carbonyl arrangement.

Measure para-bromoacetophenone m30 at 50/1 and 100 ul, predicted 25.03/52.05. Its measured 10/1 anchor 2420964caf34a1de2a5d is 8.96/23.37. The selected para-fluoro curve and measured ortho-bromo high-ratio anchor afa41ea119c8062d57fa test whether halogen and substitution-position response corrections transfer appropriately.

Measure para-fluoroacetophenone m34 at 10/1 and 100 ul, predicted 9.28/26.87. Its 5/1 observation 059b09a46d0835771fd6 is 7.72/15.54 at 50 ul. This anchors the selected 50/1 extension at constant loading and enables a direct condition comparison with measured m30 at 10/1, while retaining density differences.

Measure m34 at 50/1 and 100 ul, predicted 14.37/40.28. The selected 10/1 condition tests its own slope, and selected m30 at 50/1 tests para-halogen transfer. The much shallower measured m65 response in fd73bcb28ed4a4959b1f and 5307ce95bcee2886afe0 cautions against a generic fluorinated-ketone correction.

Measure aryl pinacol boronate m62 at 10/1 and 50 ul, predicted 3.72/8.69. Its measured 5/1 anchor 899e3f4f8af9b2c20b3b is 5.28/7.83 at 100 ul. This anchors a fixed-loading pair with selected 50/1 on a sparsely supervised boron-containing graph; the pair avoids conflating ratio and amount.

Extend m62 to 50/1 and 50 ul, predicted 8.53/25.44, with CW percentile 0.979. Selected 10/1 tests whether the predicted delayed finish growth is supported. This provides condition-response coverage for a boronate environment poorly represented by ordinary ether and ester analogies; CW is supporting evidence rather than proof of error.

Measure aromatic chloroketone m169 at 50/1 and 100 ul, predicted 14.49/40.11. Its matched 20/1 anchor a8313da6e9c9be0c1636 is 6.56/24.31. This tests whether aromatic substitution supports finish growth absent from the recent aliphatic m27 curve, helping prevent its failure repair from transferring too broadly.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response slopes and curvature depend strongly on scaffold, and V1 and V2 can respond differently. Increasing PE/EA does not justify imposing a universal monotonic endpoint correction on these catalog observations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled interior labels teach graph-dependent response functions and distinguish onset displacement from finish growth. They also bound the influence of unexpectedly short or nonmonotonic observations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m95 develop its late finish, does m27 recover finish growth at 20/1, and where does m68's measured finish decrease occur?

hypotheses.content: Recorded DCM loading-volume associations for m125 depend on mobile-phase ratio and endpoint. Large finish differences at 1/1 and 2/1 diminish at 5/1, while onset differences at 5/1 remain sensitive to sample amount. These are associations within the supplied conditions, not an established mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor remains nearly insensitive to loading volume. A stronger-eluent boundary label can teach when this feature association should diminish instead of applying one correction across ratios.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: In neat EA at 50 ul, does changing recorded DCM volume from 300 to 500 ul materially alter either endpoint?

hypotheses.content: Sample-amount sensitivity is scaffold- and ratio-dependent and can be much stronger for onset than finish. The ordered m135 and m94 series support local relationships; irregular m81 measurements limit transfer of a universal loading law.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific supervision can repair the weak learned amount dependence without forcing onset and finish to share one adjustment. Matched amount contrasts help determine how far a newly acquired condition correction should propagate.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m27's short 10/1 finish persist at higher amount, and do the aminobenzonitrile response slopes change when sample amount increases?

hypotheses.content: Detailed carbonyl environment, conjugation, substitution position and ester-side-chain structure can limit retention-response transfer between related molecules. Similar descriptors or fingerprints do not establish equivalent endpoint curves.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related-scaffold condition contrasts test whether QGeoGNN shares response information appropriately across common ketone, aldehyde and ester rows. They can repair both excessive and insufficient transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do acetoacetate ester variants retain distinct intermediate-ratio responses, and do methoxy, acetate and halogen substitutions support their predicted carbonyl response differences?

hypotheses.content: At 50 ul, both aminobenzonitrile positional isomers show steep increases from 2/1 to 5/1. The earlier predicted finish decreases were contradicted by measurement. Their response directions agree, while their 5/1 magnitudes differ; transfer across amount remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These were the largest recent acquisition-time failures. Higher-amount local curves test whether retraining learned a transferable structure-condition relationship or a correction confined to the acquired rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the steep 2/1-to-5/1 response persist for m160 at 150 ul and m161 at 100 ul, and where does positional divergence begin at 50 ul?

hypotheses.content: The current predictor gives unmeasured response valleys for m197, m209 and m190: selected higher-PE conditions are predicted to finish earlier than their selected 2/1 conditions. These may be additional shared response-shape errors, but the aminobenzonitrile outcome does not establish the answer for phenolic graphs.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched pairs discriminate a recurring functional approximation error from genuine scaffold-specific catalog behavior. Testing several related phenolic environments reveals whether any correction should transfer across hydroxyl-carbonyl geometry and fluorinated ether substitution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the measured endpoints decline from 2/1 to the selected higher ratios, and is the direction shared across these three phenolic environments?

feedback_interpretation: The aminobenzonitrile matrix overturned the proposed real finish decrease: m160 rose from 14.14/34.07 at 2/1 to 44.72/101.17 at 5/1, and m161 from 14.22/31.49 to 34.93/86.44. Their acquisition-time finish underpredictions at 5/1 were 84.81 and 72.02 mL. Current predictions now represent late 5/1 elution, so the next useful question is transfer across amount and the lower-ratio positional relationship. The m95 50/1 finish of 75.76, versus its acquisition prediction of 26.32, motivates interior labels and close acetoacetate comparisons. Conversely, m27 at 10/1 measured 4.67/6.01 after a 20.69/40.98 prediction, and m201 at 50/1 remained only 6.47/20.02. These outcomes argue against selecting large predicted growth as though it were observed retention. The m67 pair confirmed a steep response, while m68's measured finish actually shortened between 5/1 and 20/1, supporting scaffold-specific curves. The m125 results sharpen the loading-volume hypothesis: at 1/1 and 150 ul, finish was 39.38 with 500 ul DCM versus 20.23 with 300 ul; at 5/1, finish differences were small at both newly compared amounts, although onset differences remained. The complete m135 5/1 series showed onset decreasing from 24.27 to 20.92 to 18.55 with amount while finish stayed near 34; m94 likewise had much smaller amount sensitivity at 5/1 than at 20/1. At 50/1, m164 and m165 finished at 68.68 and 30.40 despite related conjugated ketone structures, strengthening the case for careful structural transfer tests. The m23 measurements were ordered with nearly unchanged onset, confirming a prediction-ordering problem rather than reversed physical elution; I do not spend further labels there this round. The m57 20/1 result stayed early, m127's 20/1 finish remained near 31 mL at low amount, and m45 showed ordinary late retention at 20/1. These findings further restrict the scope of the anomalous high-ratio records. Historical errors above refer to acquisition time, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 labels form interpretable comparisons across 18 scaffolds. Five aminobenzonitrile experiments test transfer after the largest recent failures; five acetoacetate-family experiments locate missing response growth and compare ester environments. The m27 contrasts bound an unexpectedly shallow response and test amount dependence. One m125 label probes the stronger-eluent boundary of a measured loading-volume association. Six phenolic experiments test currently predicted valleys without assuming that the aminobenzonitrile result generalizes to them, while the m68 midpoint investigates a valley already supported by neighboring measurements. Methoxy carbonyl, formyl-acetate, para-halogenated ketone and aromatic chloroketone labels address common structural transfer relationships, with controlled pairs where available. The boronate pair explores a sparsely supervised graph through a fixed-loading response experiment. No duplicate condition tuples are selected together. The batch emphasizes relationships that can supervise many remaining rows, including separate onset and finish responses, rather than maximizing retention or repeating already well-constrained regions. Density-times-volume amounts are retained when comparing compounds; missing experimental context and irregular observations limit causal interpretation. All selections and supplied predictions are fixed before any new measurement is revealed.
